packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
UNVERIFIED IMAGE-ONLY READING — packet 09

Inputs confined to this packet's prompt, metadata and two supplied images. No external source or proposed identification was consulted or exposed.

Layout survey
Both photographs are upright. Each shows a leaf laid against a binding board, written in two narrow columns in brown ink with a wide intervening gutter. Image-001 has a fairly continuous text in both columns; image-002 has a conspicuous blank interval in the right column after its first short block. There are no securely distinguished running titles, colored rubrics, or decorative enlarged initials. Some sentence beginnings use a larger capital; numerous long horizontal strokes are abbreviation strokes or flourishes, not demonstrable underlining. Small extensions enter the margins, but I cannot securely separate a marginal commentary from ordinary line extensions. The hand is exceptionally heavily abbreviated. A small surface loss interrupts image-001's upper right text. The two photographs are distinct text surfaces, not overlapping crops.

Selection and transcription
No legible heading is apparent. I selected the opening of the right column of image-001 and the opening of the left column of image-002. Column lines are numbered from their first written line at the top of the original image. Unresolved abbreviations are left as approximations of the visible letter group and stroke; expansions, where proposed, are in parentheses. These samples are incomplete and should be checked directly against the images.

Sample A — image-001.jpg, right column:

The split forma / līz? is reproduced across the physical line break; I am not asserting a completed word. Neither sample yielded a sufficiently certain continuous sentence. The fragments retain their surrounding line sequence to make checking possible. There is no visually secure lemma/commentary division within these selections. No deletion or interlinear insertion can be confidently identified.

Inspection/transforms
Viewed both whole images. Original dimensions: image-001 3539 × 4820; image-002 3455 × 4757. Native crops: image-001 left upper region approximately (813,602)–(1911,1566), image-002 left upper region (449,594)–(1692,1546), and image-001 right upper region (1980,620)–(3210,1500). No rotations, filtering, contrast changes, or restoration. Crops overlap the full photographs and were not counted as additional text.

Limitations/unread areas
Most of both columns below the selected openings remains unread. Image-001's upper left was inspected but not sufficiently resolved to include as a passage. The photographs are sharp enough to show individual strokes, but dense cursive abbreviations leave my transcription low-confidence. A specialist second image-only reading would be more valuable than automatic expansion. No missing text has been filled from a hypothesized source.
